name: Typefaces, fonts and type licences
one_line: A proposed typeface-production and font-distribution situation; refused because the current creative schema has no fields and the evidence is already an asset value, a file format, or a licensing-rights record.
refuse_reason: The row does not survive the template node test. A font family/style is a value read from a font's metadata; .otf/.ttf/.woff are file formats; and an EULA, purchase receipt, or rights schedule is licensing-rights evidence. The only potentially distinct situation would be a typeface-production/version/distribution graph containing source glyphs, build configuration, generated binaries, specimen output, and a licence or release record. That graph is not represented by any field in the placeholder creative schema (fields: []), so this row cannot recommend a legal dimension order or write a creative fact. Route governed reusable font packages to creative.stock-asset-library, rights instruments to creative.licensing-rights, handoff-embedded fonts to creative.deliverable-handoff, and otherwise to residuals.

deterministic: a font binary whose internal name table exposes family/style/vendor metadata; this proves a font file, not a typeface-production project or licence

a source/build graph in which glyph sources, feature files, a build configuration, generated binaries, and specimen output are all linked by the same family/version identity; this is a possible production signal but cannot activate a creative fact while the schema declares no fields
a licence or purchase record naming the family beside the governed font members; this is rights/asset evidence, not a distinct creative template
needs_llm: deciding whether a family directory is a type designer's source project, a purchased reusable library, an installed-font backup, or a client handoff
matching a specimen PDF and build output to the same family/version when filenames differ
separating a bespoke typeface commissioned for a brand identity from a third-party font merely used in that identity
never_alone: a family or foundry name in a filename, PDF, email, or prose; common names and vendor names occur in unrelated design and legal material
a font file by itself: presence does not distinguish designed source, licensed asset, embedded handoff member, application installation, or backup
a version token such as v2, R3, beta, release, or final without a linked source/build/output chain

grouping_reasons: one type family across source, build outputs, styles, specimens, and release versions
one governed asset package with its acquisition and rights records
one delivery package containing fonts embedded with the creative handoff
one brand identity project and its bespoke typeface when the same evidence supports both groups

template.why: Empty by contract and by refusal. The creative schema declares no fields, so typeface, style, foundry, licence class, and source format cannot become dimensions here. A family/style order would be a private schema; a provider/licence order belongs to the stock-asset or licensing-rights situation; a project-first order belongs to the consuming creative project or handoff. The user may later adopt an existing canonical field set, but this row cannot decide that.

a matching build configuration and generated binaries are present
must_not_conclude: that the source is a client commission
a creative field while creative declares none

must_not_conclude: a typeface name as a destination fact

must_not_conclude: that it is not embedded in a handoff

must_not_conclude: a typeface project from format alone

a family fact from OCR alone

repository manifest identifies the package
must_not_conclude: that the repository is a typeface domain rather than code
a family name from a variable

collides_with.signal: AcmeSans-Bold.otf plus AcmeSans-EULA.pdf can be either a governed reusable font asset or a typeface-production set; the distinction is a catalogue/acquisition/rights pairing versus source glyphs and a reproducible build graph. The binary alone is mutex evidence.
AcmeSans-EULA.pdf and Order-4821-AcmeSans.eml are rights instruments and acquisition evidence, not type design; this proposed row must not absorb them merely because they name a family.
Brand_Rebrand_Fonts_Handoff.zip contains font members as part of a recipient package; package manifest/receipt/custody evidence makes handoff primary, not font production.
build-fonts.py and a repository manifest are code-project evidence; a build script is not a typeface node unless the linked source/output graph is itself the organizing situation.

sensitivity_why: Font packages and build files can expose unreleased type designs, client identities, vendor orders, source paths, and licence restrictions. This is a privacy posture only; it is not a handling class and does not create a field or destination.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: decide whether typeface production should become a future creative template only after the creative schema adopts existing canonical project/stage/artifact fields, or whether it remains a value/work type under creative. Separately decide whether font licence scope belongs exclusively to creative.licensing-rights or may be searchable metadata on stock assets. Until that decision, no typeface, style, foundry, source_format, or licence_class field is proposed.
